Photocurrent went up steadily as the composition became more V-rich: idx110 (Bi-rich) gave 1.5e-6 A, idx34 gave 1.26e-5 A and idx0 (Bi0.36 Cu0.18 V0.46) gave 2.65e-5 A, the highest measured.

content.text:
I submitted **index 0** (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46). At 2.65×10⁻⁵ A it gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured. I don't know how close it is to the library's best: that was probably not reached.

I only had 3 photocurrent measurements, so I aimed them at compositions near BiVO₄ (roughly equal Bi and V, little Cu). BiVO₄ is the usual visible-light photoanode material, which makes it the best-supported bet at this light energy (2.72 eV).

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 110 | 0.47 / 0.19 / 0.34 | 1.5×10⁻⁶ |
| 34 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 1.26×10⁻⁵ |
| 0 | 0.36 / 0.18 / 0.46 | 2.65×10⁻⁵ |

- **The trend hadn't levelled off:** photocurrent roughly doubled or better with each step towards more V. More V-rich compositions such as index 29 (Bi 0.32, V 0.51) could well be better, but the budget ran out before I could test them.
- **Cu-rich compositions were never measured.** I skipped them on the assumption that they perform worse, which is untested.
- **The structure measurements went unused:** I didn't spend any of the 5, so the choice rests only on composition and prior knowledge, not on identified phases.
